parameters.content:
## Log automated decisions and route Article 22 review requests

### How it works
Two forms and a weekly check. The first form logs a decision a system made about a person. A Code node applies the Article 22(1) test as it is actually written: the decision must be BOTH solely automated AND have a legal or similarly significant effect, and only then do the Article 22(2) exceptions matter. Eight effects live in a data table you can edit; each Yes answer and each keyword in the decision text counts one. A sign-off that cannot change the outcome is treated as solely automated, which is what the WP29 guidance says. A Groq call may add an effect only by quoting the decision word for word, and a suggestion without a real quote is discarded. The verdict is one of ART22_SAFEGUARDS_REQUIRED, ART22_NO_LAWFUL_BASIS, NOT_SOLELY_AUTOMATED, NO_SIGNIFICANT_EFFECT or INCOMPLETE. The second form is for the person: it looks the decision up in the register, sets the one month Article 12(3) deadline, and records the request. A reference that is not in the register gives INCOMPLETE, never "nothing to review". Every Monday the workflow reports decisions still without safeguards and requests past their deadline.

### Setup
1. Add a Groq credential to the Groq node and a Discord webhook to both Discord nodes.
2. Run Set Up Tables once. It creates four tables and loads the eight effects.
3. Log a test decision, then use the second form with that reference and with a reference that does not exist.

### Customization tips
Edit the effects and keywords in art22_effect_rules; the table is the policy. Set safeguards_documented to yes on a register row once the safeguards exist. Keywords are English. This is a triage aid, not legal advice.

## 1. Create the tables and load the eight effects (run once)
Four tables are created with typed columns, or reused when the names exist. The eight effects are upserted by key, so a second run changes nothing. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. Log a decision and apply the two limbs
The [form](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.formtrigger/) records the decision. Set Article 22 Policy holds the valid bases. Both limbs must hold before Art. 22 bites, and a sign-off that changes nothing counts as automated.

## 3. Review and decide
The [LLM Chain](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/) may add an effect only with a verbatim quote checked against the decision text. It can raise the verdict and can never lower it.

## 4. Record the decision
One row per decision in art22_decisions with the verdict and safeguards_documented set to no, one row per effect in art22_effect_findings, or a none row so every decision leaves a trace.

## 5. Escalate and answer
A decision needing safeguards or with no valid basis goes to [Discord](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.discord/), then the logger sees the verdict page. Swap Discord for Slack or Gmail.

## 6. The person asks for a human
The second form looks the reference up in the register. Found means OPEN with a one month deadline. Not found, no reference or an empty register all mean INCOMPLETE and the request still stands.

## 7. Weekly outstanding check
The [Schedule Trigger](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger/) reads both tables and reports decisions still without safeguards and requests past the Art. 12(3) deadline. Two empty tables are reported as nothing logged.
